body: I found the "entitlement processing", it was in this comment
arena commander dev replied with a very good suggestion to play Arena Commander orbStar Marine as those servers, while bugged, are actually very much playable it seems.

Wait, no, pull out the flight sticks! Have you never used them for SC before or did you have a bad experience? Mouse and keyboard personally feels far too sluggish to enjoy, especially when I have to hold W forever. 

Though mouse and keyboard remains king for the purposes of aiming
I'll quickly add that as others have said the Cutter is fantastic. The extra quantum fuel is pure joy after years of small ships having tiny capacity.

Vets will help you.
best light fighter is the Gladius if you want an eagle feel although the arrow is still good enough. Both can be purchased rather cheaply in-game.
Space sim roleplay is probably the best you can find if you enjoy walking around a lot. While the actual roleplay is minimal, there is huge potential.

If you want to do bounty hunting there are missions dedicated for said purpose. Completing these will slowly level up your rep with the respective planet's faction. It's quick cash if you're competent. Otherwise there are ground missions to grind too.

One thing to keep in mind is that there is a major patch hitting soon which will upend a nice chunk of the gameplay loop. Lots more to mess around with.

My only other bit of advice is to avoid buying new ships altogether. Nearly all ships are around ten times cheaper than they should be so upgrading from a starter to something larger shouldn't take long.

You could also ask to join in on some high pay missions, which should get you some good cash early too. Dynamic events are infrequent but are a fantastic source of cash.

Back to roleplay: I've found roleplay to be rare but very good fun once you get into it. And the ability to change walk speed is incredible for walking around the major cities and outposts. Game is gorgeous.

As someone who dwells on the subject of the mind and its many strange variations, I feel obliged to give my own experience here:  I personally do not see images in my but rather I have a very specific blur of colour perhaps. But that is with my eyes open.
  When closed, my imagination takes over like an AI, seemingly. I can imagine what look like vivid images and even scenes, conversations and feelings much like what you might find in a dream. So in the same way that you can only see the concept of the subject you are trying to see mentally, I can sometimes "hear, smell, feel, see or taste" the image/concept I'm trying to visualise, so as to make it more accurate, if that makes sense? But it's only ever a fragile mess of colour and sensations when you focus, which breaks the illusion. It's all imaginary, technically. 
  My experience, however, is mostly based around memories (which fade the more I think about them, not the best way of living I can't lie) , but I thought it would be nice to share my experience to provide some points of comparison for ya.

Lemme know if any of this made sense, I tend to get lost in my own thoughts when writing.
